//: Type-check the JavaScript, without migrating anything to TypeScript.
The page object layer added in phase 6 moved risk out of the specs and into a layer of
objects whose every locator is a property reached by name. A typo there is not a syntax
error: app.day.tickk('x') evaluates to undefined, and undefined.click() then fails deep
inside a test with a message about the test rather than about the typo. Nothing in the
repository could see that class of defect before the layer existed, and nothing moved in
checkJs turns Playwright's own shipped types into a check over the harness. It reads the
same files eslint already reads and needs no annotation in them.
The harness only. Not public/, not src/: the application is a single inlined build written
in another style, and pointing a type checker at it would produce noise nobody asked for.
Deliberately short of strict. strictNullChecks would flag every locator chain that Playwright
types as possibly null, which is most of them, and the answer would be assertions written to
satisfy the checker rather than to describe the app. The setting that earns its place here is
the one that catches a name that does not exist.
